source: Per-company AR extraction (Screener.in PDFs + IR sites) — Claude.ai routine, daily batch of 20

rural.evidence: Radico Khaitan sells IMFL brands across India including semi-urban and rural markets. Economy and mid-priced segments (Contessa rum, Old Admiral brandy) have rural/semi-urban reach. Prestige & Above portfolio targeted at urban premium consumers. Rural revenue % not separately disclosed in available MD&A.

inr_exposure.evidence: Radico Khaitan exports premium IMFL brands (Rampur Single Malt, Jaisalmer Indian Craft Gin, Magic Moments) to 100+ countries. Export revenue accounts for approximately 9–10% of IMFL revenue per management commentary and research reports. IMFL revenue ₹3,371.7 Cr = 69.5% of FY25 total sales. FY25 net revenue ~₹4,851 Cr (+~20% YoY; FY26 net revenue confirmed at ₹6,050 Cr, implying FY25 ~₹4,851 Cr). Exports primarily in USD and GBP to duty-free channels and international distributors.

govt_capex.evidence: BEL is a Navratna Defence PSU under Ministry of Defence. FY25 provisional turnover ₹23,000 Cr (+16% YoY from ₹19,820 Cr in FY24). Revenue is ~90%+ from Indian defence forces (Army, Navy, Air Force), DRDO, MoD-linked programmes. FY25 export order book $359 million; order inflows FY25 ₹18,715 Cr vs target of ₹25,000 Cr. Order book as of April 2025 at ₹71,650 Cr. Products: radars, communication systems, electronic warfare, avionics, solar, electro-optics.

rate_sensitive.evidence: BEL is effectively debt-free. As a Navratna PSU with strong operating cash flows (FY25 revenue ₹23,000 Cr, EBITDA margin ~25%), BEL carries zero meaningful interest-bearing external debt and has no floating rate liability exposure.

inr_exposure.evidence: FY25 export sales $106 million (~₹895 Cr) vs $92.98 million in FY24 (+14% YoY). Total FY25 revenue ~₹23,000 Cr. Export share ~3.9%. Export order book $359 million as of April 2025. Key export destinations: Israel, ASEAN, Middle East for defence electronics and systems. USD-denominated export orders.

pli_scheme.evidence: BEL is a Central PSU under Ministry of Defence. PLI schemes are designed to incentivise private sector capital investment. PSUs like BEL are not designated PLI beneficiaries. Defence sector PLI applies to private Indian defence manufacturers.

china_plus_one.evidence: ABB India annual report 2025 states: 'higher share of service and export revenues contributed to margin expansion.' ABB India's Distribution Solutions division exports to global ABB entities and international customers. Export growth is cited as margin-enhancing but no explicit China+1 narrative found in available AR excerpts. ABB India is primarily a domestic-market-facing industrial automation and electrification company.

govt_capex.evidence: ABB India serves infrastructure, railways, power distribution (Electrification segment), and process industries (Process Automation). Key govt/infrastructure end-markets: data centers, EPC customers, renewable energy projects, railway electrification, power T&D. Orders surged to ₹3,607 Cr in Q1 FY25 (5-year high); order backlog ₹9,380 Cr (+12% YoY as of Dec 2024). FY25 annual revenue ~₹12,088 Cr (+~16-20% YoY). Government infra capex is a primary demand driver but exact revenue % from govt projects not disclosed.

inr_exposure.evidence: ABB India export revenue was less than 10% of total in recent years per disclosed commentary ('export revenues <10% in Q4 FY23'). FY25 annual revenue ~₹12,088 Cr. Export ~7% (~₹847 Cr) primarily from Distribution Solutions and inter-company transfers to ABB Group entities. USD/EUR denominated exports.

rural.evidence: Nykaa's eB2B distribution business (Superstore by Nykaa) reaches ~260,000 transacting retailers across 1,100+ cities, including tier-2/3 cities. However, rural India is not a primary revenue driver; the business is predominantly urban and semi-urban. No separate rural revenue % disclosed.

inr_exposure.evidence: Nykaa operates predominantly as a domestic Indian e-commerce beauty retailer. Q3 FY25 consolidated revenue ₹2,267 Cr (+27% YoY); FY25 full-year revenue estimated ~₹8,000–8,500 Cr. International revenue is negligible (<1% of consolidated) from early-stage international expansion to Middle East. No material USD-denominated revenue.

china_plus_one.evidence: Bosch India exports automotive components globally (principally to Bosch Group entities in Germany, Japan, and other markets) as part of the global Bosch Group supply chain. This is structural rather than a China+1 repositioning. Domestic sales grew 6.2% in FY25; export sales also grew under Powertrain Solutions division. No explicit China+1 framing in available MD&A/press release.

inr_exposure.evidence: Bosch India FY25 total revenue ₹18,087 Cr (+8.1% YoY). Export revenue approximately 25% of total (~₹4,522 Cr), primarily inter-company transfers to Bosch GmbH and international Bosch Group entities. Revenue sectors: Mobility (domestic automotive OEM + exports + aftermarket) ~88%, Beyond Mobility (power tools, consumer goods) ~12%. Domestic auto OEM grew 6.2%; export auto segment also grew. USD + EUR revenue estimated ~20% of total (international component exports).

pli_scheme.evidence: Bosch Limited is confirmed among the 75 companies that received PLI approval under the PLI Scheme for Automobile and Auto Components (Component Champion Incentive Scheme approved by Ministry of Heavy Industries on March 15, 2022). Bosch India manufactures EVS-eligible components including EV powertrain systems, advanced driver assistance systems (ADAS), and automotive electronics. PLI incentive revenue not separately disclosed in FY25.

china_plus_one.evidence: Royal Enfield is expanding its international presence as an 'accessible premium' motorcycle brand at the $2,000–$5,000 price point where Chinese brands are weak. International volumes surged 29.7% to 100,136 units in FY25 (highest ever). CKD assembly plants opened in Thailand and announced in Brazil. Bangladesh manufacturing facility opened. The company competes with Chinese motorcycles in SE Asia and LATAM on quality and brand positioning, benefitting from India's motorcycle manufacturing credentials as a credible alternative to Chinese brands.

rural.evidence: VECV (VE Commercial Vehicles, Eicher's truck/bus JV with Volvo) serves rural India logistics, agriculture transport, and construction. Royal Enfield's lower-priced models (Bullet 350, Meteor) serve semi-urban and tier-3 markets. Rural revenue % not separately disclosed for the consolidated entity.

inr_exposure.evidence: Eicher Motors FY25 consolidated revenue ₹18,870 Cr (+14.1% YoY). Royal Enfield domestic 902,757 units (90%), exports 100,136 units (10% by volume, +29.7% YoY). VECV (trucks/buses) is predominantly domestic. Export revenue at ~premium realization; USD/EUR-denominated export estimated ~8-10% of consolidated revenue (~₹1,510–1,887 Cr).

pli_scheme.evidence: Eicher Motors / Royal Enfield was not found among named PLI beneficiaries under the Automobile and Auto Components PLI scheme. The scheme primarily targets EV powertrain, advanced auto components, and EV battery manufacturers. Royal Enfield's product mix (ICE motorcycles) does not align with the PLI scheme's EV focus.

rural.evidence: Pidilite has strong rural distribution for Fevicol and M-Seal through India's building materials distribution network. AR notes 'Emerging India' growth segment (semi-urban + rural) outperforming urban markets. Q3 FY25 commentary noted 'subdued demand across urban and rural geographies.' Rural market is material but specific revenue % not disclosed.

govt_capex.evidence: Pidilite's B2B construction chemicals (waterproofing, industrial adhesives) serve infrastructure projects including roads, bridges, metro, and affordable housing — partially government-linked. Specific govt capex revenue % not disclosed.

crude_exposure.evidence: Vinyl Acetate Monomer (VAM), a key raw material for PVA and emulsion adhesives, is derived from acetic acid and ethylene — both crude/natural gas linked. VAM is a material input for Pidilite's adhesive portfolio. Pidilite's own risk disclosures mention crude-linked RM price risk but exact % of RM cost from crude derivatives not disclosed.

inr_exposure.evidence: Pidilite FY25 consolidated revenue ₹13,400 Cr (+~14% YoY). International subsidiaries (USA: Pidilite USA; Brazil: Pulvitec; Middle East, Africa, South Asia) contributed ~16% of consolidated revenue (~₹2,144 Cr). B2B export segment also growing (+18% UVG in Q1 FY25). USD revenue estimated ~10% (USA subsidiary + Middle East exports); balance is BRL, BDT, AED.

china_plus_one.evidence: Lupin's CDMO business grew 49% YoY in FY25 as global innovators diversify API/synthesis manufacturing from China. Lupin is positioned as an alternative to Chinese API suppliers for global pharma. Integrated Report 2024-25 cites supply chain resilience and CDMO capability as growth drivers. Other developed markets revenue +23.4% YoY reflects diversification gains. 70 US DMFs filed; multiple USFDA, EMA-approved manufacturing sites.

inr_exposure.evidence: Lupin FY25 consolidated revenue INR 227,079 Mn = ₹22,707 Cr (+13.5% YoY). Geographic mix: India ~31% (~₹7,039 Cr); US ~31% (~₹7,039 Cr, $925 Mn at ~₹84/USD); Other Developed Markets (Europe, Australia, Japan) ~11% (₹2,498 Cr); Emerging Markets ~11–14%; API ~5%. Total export ~69%. Of total sale ₹164,585.8 Mn, 53.9% export per financial statements standalone figure. USD revenue estimated ~42% (US formulations + US-denominated API contracts + partial EM markets).

pli_scheme.evidence: Lupin is a confirmed beneficiary under the PLI Scheme for Bulk Drugs — covering Key Starting Materials (KSMs), Drug Intermediates (DIs), and Active Pharmaceutical Ingredients (APIs). The scheme aims to reduce India's API import dependence on China. PLI incentive income not separately disclosed but facilities are PLI-approved.

china_plus_one.evidence: Navin Fluorine competes directly with Chinese fluorochemical manufacturers globally. The specialty chemicals and CRAMS/CDMO segments serve global pharma companies (agrochemicals, pharmaceuticals) diversifying their fluorine chemistry supply chains away from China. CRAMS/CDMO revenue grew 141% YoY in Q4 FY25, driven by multi-year contracts from MNC pharma companies seeking non-Chinese supply. HPP (High Performance Products) segment also serves global chemical companies using fluorine intermediates. FY25 total revenue ₹2,393 Cr; CRAMS/CDMO ~18% of revenue and growing fastest. Global fluorochemical customers are explicitly seeking Indian alternatives to Chinese suppliers.

crude_exposure.evidence: Navin Fluorine's primary raw material is Hydrofluoric Acid (HF) derived from Fluorspar (a mineral ore), not crude oil. Some petroleum-based solvents used in CRAMS/CDMO processes but no material crude-linked raw material cost. Fluorspar price and availability is the primary RM risk.

inr_exposure.evidence: Navin Fluorine FY25 revenue ₹2,393 Cr. Export ~70% (~₹1,675 Cr), primarily from Specialty Chemicals (~35-40% of total, ~75% exports), HPP/CRAMS (~18-20%, ~90% exports), Inorganic Fluorides (partially exported). Domestic: Refrigerants (~15-20%) and domestic specialty chemical sales. USD revenue estimated ~60% of total — export contracts with global pharma/specialty chem companies predominantly USD-denominated.

pli_scheme.evidence: No PLI scheme currently covers specialty fluorochemicals. The Specialty Chemicals PLI scheme was under consideration by MoC&F but not launched as of FY25. Navin Fluorine is not a confirmed PLI beneficiary.

govt_capex.evidence: Siemens India's Smart Infrastructure segment (switchgear, power transformers, building automation) and Mobility segment (rail electrification, signalling) primarily serve government/regulated utilities and Indian Railways. Large government-linked programmes: railway electrification, metro rail, power T&D upgrades, and renewable energy grid integration. Order backlog ₹42,845 Cr (+8% YoY) as of Q3 FY25 (Feb 2025). Siemens India's FY24 revenue (Oct 2023–Sep 2024): ₹20,250 Cr. Government and infrastructure capex is a dominant end-market (~50–60% of order intake) but exact revenue % not disclosed.

inr_exposure.evidence: Siemens India (fiscal year ends September 30) FY2024 (Oct 2023–Sep 2024) revenue ₹20,250 Cr. Primarily domestic-market-facing company — automation, electrification, and digital industries for Indian customers. Export revenue ~7% (~₹1,418 Cr), mainly inter-company transfers to Siemens AG entities and some direct exports of switchgear/automation products. USD revenue estimated ~6% of total.

rural.evidence: Nippon Life India AMC has geographical presence at 271 locations pan-India including B-30 cities (beyond top 30 by AUM). SEBI mandates B-30 investor outreach; retail AUM includes investors from semi-urban towns. Rural/B-30 AUM share growing but not separately disclosed as revenue %.

rate_sensitive.evidence: Nippon Life India AMC is an asset-light company with no meaningful debt. It generates management fee revenue based on AUM (₹5.89+ lakh crore as of March 2025). Floating rate liability % is effectively 0. Rate changes affect AUM indirectly through equity/debt fund flows but company's own balance sheet has no floating rate borrowing.

inr_exposure.evidence: Nippon Life India AMC manages Indian mutual fund schemes in INR. Revenue is 100% INR-denominated management fees. Singapore subsidiary (NAM Singapore) manages offshore India-focused funds but this is a small fraction of total AUM and revenue. AUM ₹5.89+ lakh crore as of March 2025; FY25 annual revenue approximately ₹2,000–2,200 Cr. No USD-denominated revenue in consolidated P&L.

china_plus_one.evidence: Sun Pharma has limited explicit China+1 narrative in FY25 AR. Specialty dermatology brands (Ilumya, Cequa, Winlevi) and branded generics compete globally. Some API and generic formulation diversification narrative in context of global pharma supply chain resilience but not a primary strategic theme.

inr_exposure.evidence: Sun Pharma FY25 consolidated revenue ₹52,041 Cr (+~9% YoY; ~US$6.2B). Geographic mix: US ~30% (₹15,612 Cr; US formulation sales $1,921 Mn +3.6% YoY); India ~30% (₹15,612 Cr, India formulation sales +13.8% YoY); Emerging Markets ~17% (US$277 Mn/quarter ~₹9,000 Cr annual); Rest of World ~23%. Export = ~70%. USD revenue estimated ~43% of total (US segment + USD-priced EM markets). Specialty brands (Ilumya, Cequa) in US generate premium USD revenue.

pli_scheme.evidence: Sun Pharmaceutical Industries is a beneficiary under the PLI Scheme for Pharmaceuticals (covering both Critical KSMs/APIs and formulations). Government PLI approval covers Sun Pharma's manufacturing of select critical APIs and advanced chemistry cell products. PLI incentive income not separately disclosed in FY25 results.

rate_sensitive.evidence: IHCL has ongoing debt for hotel capex and renovations. Hotels and hospitality companies typically carry term loans and working capital facilities with floating rate components. EBITDA margin expanded to 43.9% in FY25. Specific floating rate liability % not disclosed in available press releases.

inr_exposure.evidence: IHCL FY25 consolidated revenue ₹8,565 Cr. IHCL Standalone (India-only hotels) ₹5,145 Cr = ~60% of consolidated. International subsidiaries (UK — Taj Hotels; USA — Pierre Hotel; Maldives; Africa; Sri Lanka) contribute ~35-40% of consolidated revenue (~₹2,997–3,422 Cr). EBITDA margin 43.9% FY25. PAT ₹1,413 Cr (+29% YoY). International portfolio: 570 hotels, 4 continents, 14 countries. USD/GBP revenue from UK and US properties estimated ~25% of consolidated.

govt_capex.evidence: KSB India supplies pumps and valves to power plants (thermal and nuclear), water treatment infrastructure, petrochemical refineries, and chemical plants — sectors with significant government capex. Orders secured include a major export order for Algeria's Hassi Massoud Refinery and water segment orders from KSB Pumps Arabia (UAE). Domestic power and water sectors are primary govt-linked end-markets. Exact revenue % not disclosed.

inr_exposure.evidence: KSB India FY25 annual revenue ₹2,696 Cr (+6.4% YoY). Export revenue approximately 15–18% of total (~₹404–485 Cr), from project exports to Middle East (Algeria, Saudi Arabia, UAE) and international KSB Group supply. Sinnar plant expanded to cater to growing export demand. USD revenue estimated ~12% of total.

Caplin Point Laboratories derives ~90% of revenues from exports. Geographic mix: Latin America 76% of total revenue (key markets: Guatemala, Honduras, El Salvador, Nicaragua, Bolivia, Ecuador); Africa 6%; US regulated market growing (~5%); domestic ~10% (forming domestic injectable sales team). End-to-end model: owns manufacturing + distribution network in LatAm. API sourcing: India 70%, China 30%. FY25 revenue estimated ~₹1,900 Cr (FY26 revenue ₹2,303 Cr, ~20% growth). USD revenue estimated ~65% of total — LatAm standard pricing in USD for tender and private market.

rural.evidence: Dr Lal PathLabs is expanding into Tier-III and Tier-IV towns as a strategic priority (contributing to Q4 FY25 volume growth and 81% PAT increase). Company has been establishing collection centres in smaller cities and towns. Rural and semi-urban is a stated growth avenue but specific revenue % from Tier-III/IV not disclosed.

rate_sensitive.evidence: Dr Lal PathLabs is a debt-free diagnostics company. FY25 consolidated revenue ₹2,461 Cr. Net cash positive; zero interest-bearing debt outstanding. Floating rate liability = 0%.

inr_exposure.evidence: FY25 revenue: India ₹2,443 Cr (99.3%) + Outside India ₹18.4 Cr (0.7%). Outside India revenue (~₹18 Cr) is from SAARC country patients. Revenue is 99.3% INR-denominated. No significant USD revenue or FX hedging required.

govt_capex.evidence: Astral's plumbing pipes (72% of FY25 revenue = ₹4,199 Cr) benefit from government housing schemes (PMAY, Jal Jeevan Mission for rural water supply pipelines). Infrastructure and government housing capex drives significant pipe demand. Specific govt capex revenue % not disclosed.

crude_exposure.evidence: Astral manufactures CPVC and uPVC plumbing pipes. PVC (polyvinyl chloride) and CPVC compounds are derived from ethylene dichloride and vinyl chloride monomer — both petrochemical derivatives linked to crude oil prices. Crude-linked RM exposure is material but exact % of total RM cost not disclosed.

inr_exposure.evidence: Astral FY25 consolidated revenue ₹5,832 Cr. Primarily domestic India market (plumbing pipes + adhesives). Acquired Al-Aziz Plastics (Middle East) for international expansion. Export revenue estimated ~8% (~₹467 Cr) from Middle East, Africa, and some direct exports; USD revenue ~5% of total.

rural.evidence: Titan's Sonata watch brand targets mass-market including semi-urban and rural Indian consumers. Tanishq's expansion into smaller towns and tier-2/3 cities is a growth priority (now in 600+ cities). CaratLane operates online with pan-India reach. Rural/semi-urban revenue not separately disclosed.

rate_sensitive.evidence: Jewellery purchases in India are partly financed through consumer EMI and gold loan schemes. Higher interest rates may dampen discretionary gold jewellery demand. However, Titan Company itself carries minimal corporate debt; consumer rate sensitivity impacts demand rather than company's own balance sheet floating rate liabilities.

inr_exposure.evidence: Titan FY25 consolidated revenue ₹57,818 Cr (+22% YoY). Jewellery 85% = ₹49,145 Cr; Watches ~9%; Eyewear, International ~6% combined. International operations: boutiques in UAE, UK, US targeting Indian diaspora; CaratLane Singapore; Taneira international. International revenue ~3–5% of consolidated (~₹1,734–2,891 Cr). USD revenue estimated ~4% of total.

govt_capex.evidence: Finolex Cables sells electrical and communication cables serving power T&D, rural electrification (DDUGJY, RGGVY schemes), data/telecom infrastructure, and real estate. Government infrastructure capex drives demand for both electrical and communication cables. Specific govt capex revenue % not disclosed.

crude_exposure.evidence: PVC compound (insulation and sheathing for cables) is a petroleum derivative. PVC prices track crude oil / naphtha / EDC-VCM chain. Finolex's cable segments use PVC as a primary insulation material — crude-linked RM exposure is material. Specific % of total RM cost not disclosed in available AR excerpts.

inr_exposure.evidence: Finolex Cables FY25 revenue ₹5,536 Cr (+6.7% YoY vs ₹5,190 Cr FY24). Segment mix: Electrical cables ~57%, Communication cables ~15%, Copper rods ~22%, Others ~6%. Export revenue ~9% (~₹498 Cr), primarily Middle East and Africa for electrical cables. USD revenue estimated ~8% of total.

china_plus_one.evidence: Garware Hi-Tech Films competes directly with Chinese polyester film manufacturers globally. Americas revenue grew from 33% (FY22) to 55% (Q2 FY25) of total revenue — driven significantly by US customers diversifying specialty film sourcing away from China amid tariff risk and supply chain resilience concerns. Company received PLEX Council Highest Exporter Award; exports to 100+ countries. Product mix: safety/security films (PPF, window films, solar control films) where China+1 diversification is explicit. Value-added specialty films ~87% of revenue. FY25 revenue ₹2,120 Cr (+25.8% YoY), indicating strong demand gains consistent with supply chain realignment.

crude_exposure.evidence: Garware Hi-Tech Films manufactures BOPET (biaxially oriented PET) specialty films. PET (polyethylene terephthalate) is made from PTA (purified terephthalic acid) and MEG (monoethylene glycol), both derived from crude oil via naphtha. Company has backward integration producing DMT (dimethyl terephthalate) chips. Crude-linked RM exposure is material — both PTA and MEG track crude/naphtha prices. Specific % of total RM from crude derivatives not disclosed.

inr_exposure.evidence: Garware Hi-Tech Films FY25 revenue ₹2,120 Cr. Geographic mix (Q2 FY25): Americas 55%, India 19%, ROW 26%. Export ~81% (~₹1,717 Cr). Americas (55% of revenue = ₹1,166 Cr) is predominantly USD-denominated. ROW includes Europe, Asia, Middle East (mix of EUR, USD, other). USD revenue estimated ~70% of total. Company exports to 100+ countries.
